issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an instance method addRating(stars:) (parameter label 'stars'), but the solution implements the method with a different parameter label (addRating(rating:)). Additionally, the solution's Client calls addRating(stars:), while the solution's Course defines addRating(rating:), making the solution repository internally inconsistent and likely to fail to compile. This mismatch between the intended API (stars) and the solution implementation (rating) will confuse students about the correct parameter label to use and prevents a working reference implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the parameter label across all artifacts. The simplest fix is to change the solution's Course implementation to match the problem/template signature: declare the method as func addRating(stars: Int) { ... } and use 'stars' inside the body. Alternatively, update the Client calls to match the chosen signature, but prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template (stars) so students and tests are consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template specify an instance method addRating(stars:) (external parameter name 'stars') for the Course class, but the solution's Course implementation defines the method with a different external parameter name (addRating(rating:)). Additionally, the solution's Client calls addRating(stars:), which is inconsistent with the solution Course signature. This mismatch in the external parameter label for the same conceptual operation (adding a course rating) creates a naming inconsistency that can confuse students mapping the requirement to the implementation and may cause compilation errors when comparing template, problem text, and solution code.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the external parameter name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution's Course method signature to use the 'stars' label to match the problem and template (e.g. func addRating(stars: Int) { ... }) and update the implementation accordingly. Ensure Client calls and any references use addRating(stars:) as well. Alternatively (less preferred), update problem and template to use addRating(rating:) everywhere — but pick one naming and apply it consistently across problem statement, template, and solution.
